chapter: Fats Waller, Zululand and the ideal band
title: Fats Waller and the gin
summary: Hungover, Fats asks for gin on stage; McPartland brings it on a tray.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Which reminds me, I threw something away I didn't mean to. This week his son had a memorial in the newspaper on the anniversary of his father's death.

Oh, marvelous man. Just a beautiful man. He played such beautiful organ along with great performing. He could sing and great personality. A great human being. He drank a lot. And as a matter of fact he used to have a little back room there where all us musicians were between sets while somebody else was on. He had a nice line up of oh, gin, whiskey, bourbon, scotch and brandy and things

And we had, one night Fats had been up very late and he had just gotten up. He just got up because he used to stay up very late. He just got up and he was late. Actually late. I kept padding the thing for him and he came and he had a terrible hangover. Just a frightful hangover. And I knew how he felt.

So he did have a blast before he, he had to go on right away. So he says to me, 'Jimmy,' he says, 'listen, if I get out there and I ask for some gin, bring it to me. I mean it. I mean it. I'm not kidding, Jimmy, bring it to me!' I said, 'don't worry about it, but you've got to go on now Fats. I've got to announce you.' 'Okay. Okay.'
So sure enough, he got out there and he sang, 'Sheik of Araby,' you know. Opened up and after he finished the number he says, 'Jimmy, Jimmy, bring me my gin!'

On the stage and the people thought it was, I came on. I put a towel over my arm and came out with a tray with the gin on it, the water and a glass, an empty glass. And I brought it out and I said, 'your gin sir.' And he took that gin man and he poured a glass full of it, that gin and he drank it.

And the people laughed. They thought it was part of the act. And believe me it was not part of the act. Fats needed a drink badly. (LAUGHTER). Now he never forgot that or anybody else. They never forgot, the guys who were in on the know. They knew that was going on. But that endeared me to Fats. It would anybody. He had a hangover and got the shakes you know. But a sweet man and a lovely human being. And a marvellous musician, composer and player and entertainer you know. For piano, you know, he was in the Louis Armstrong class to me as a person. Two beautiful men. Dedicated musicians. Great spirit, but their spirit lives on fortunately with their music.
